analysis.title: Investors still shaken (FX Risk Index)
key_insights: CACIB FX Risk Index at -0.6483 vs -0.8370 last week, continuing a gradual retreat from risk-seeking territory. The Index sits around its 100-day moving average, which the report says suggests the retreat could be prolonged.
Technology stocks remain under pressure despite Nvidia's earnings and forecast surprising to the upside. New US restrictions on advanced chip access, physical and remote, are worrying investors.

Data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil need a US government license before letting Chinese companies remotely access advanced AI chips and servers. They also need a license to buy advanced AI chips from Nvidia and other US manufacturers. The report says it is not specified whether US data centres face the same licensing.
Tech earnings that justify elevated valuations are being discounted at a higher rate. Strong US economic data and hawkish FOMC rhetoric have pushed UST yields back higher.
A Trump-Xi bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC Summit in Shenzhen on 19 November is expected to cover the chip restrictions and will matter for investor sentiment.
The Anthropic IPO on 19 November is another test for sentiment. The report says the offering is reportedly six times oversubscribed. Crédit Agricole CIB is joint bookrunner.
Over the past week the Index was driven higher by higher equity and FX volatility and by defensive stocks outperforming cyclicals. Lower gold prices and private-credit spreads capped the gains.
Among G10 currencies, only CHF, CAD and SEK have significant positive correlations with the Risk Index. GBP, USD and NOK have significant negative correlations.
